name: YIELDDISC
description: YIELDDISC returns the annual yield for a security that is priced at a discount, such as a Treasury bill.
tldr: Calculates the annual yield of a discounted security.

basicExample.description: Yield of a discounted Treasury bill
basicExample.explanation: A T-bill priced at $95 that redeems at $100 in one year has an annual yield of about 5.41%.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/360 basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 2 is common for money market instruments.

howItWorks: YIELDDISC calculates the annual yield using the formula (redemption - pr) / pr * (days per year / days to maturity). It is used for zero-coupon and short-term discount instruments.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Price and redemption are per $100 face value.
Basis affects the day count and year length.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: YIELDDISC works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between YIELDDISC and DISC?
faq.answer: YIELDDISC calculates yield based on price. DISC calculates the discount rate based on price.

faq.question: When is YIELDDISC used?
faq.answer: It is used for Treasury bills and other discount securities.
